description: Sclerotinia leaf rot is a fungal disease that affects many crops. The fungus infects leaves and stems under cool and wet conditions. It produces white cotton-like mold and black survival structures called sclerotia.
symptoms: Soft rot on infected leaf tissue
White cotton-like fungal growth on leaves or stems
Black seed-like sclerotia forming in infected areas
disease_cycle: The fungus survives in soil as sclerotia for several years
Sclerotia germinate and produce cup-shaped apothecia
Apothecia release spores into the air
Spores infect leaves during wet conditions
New sclerotia form on infected plants and return to soil
impact: Possible plant collapse in severe infections
cultural_control: Remove infected plant debris from fields
biological_control: Use biocontrol fungi such as Coniothyrium minitans
Use beneficial microbes like Trichoderma species
chemical_control: Apply registered fungicides when disease risk is high
Preventive fungicide sprays in humid conditions
prevention: Monitor crops during cool and wet seasons
